segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.

segments.en: And today we're at a party.

segments.en: Yeah, this is a great, exciting, fun, energetic lesson.
segments.zh: 是的，这是一个很棒的、令人兴奋的、有趣的、充满活力的课程。

segments.en: We're at the biggest party in the world, Carnival in Rio.
segments.zh: 我们参加了世界上最大的派对，里约热内卢的狂欢节。

segments.en: Okay, so Rio, this is the name of a city, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，里约，这是一个城市的名字，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, this is a city in Brazil called Rio de Janeiro.
segments.zh: 是的，这是巴西的一个叫里约热内卢的城市。

segments.en: Yeah, yours sounds a lot more, I don't know, authentic than mine.
segments.zh: 是的，你的听起来更多，我不知道，比我的真实。

segments.en: So we sometimes refer to it as Rio just to make it shorter.
segments.zh: 所以我们有时把它称为里约，只是为了让它更短。

segments.en: Yeah, I think that's actually the most common way it's referred to in English.
segments.zh: 是的，我认为这实际上是英语中最常见的方式。

segments.en: It's just like if you would say Los Angeles, you would say LA.
segments.zh: 就像你说洛杉矶，你会说洛杉矶。

segments.en: Yeah, or if you're talking about Kuala Lumpur, you might say KL.
segments.zh: 是的，或者如果你在谈论吉隆坡，你可能会说 KL。

segments.en: Okay, so we have some words that we're going to preview before we listen to our dialogue.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们有一些词要在我们听对话之前预览。

segments.zh: 所以让我们从词汇预览开始。

segments.en: Okay, in vocabulary preview, we have one word, Sambadrome.
segments.zh: 好的，在词汇预览中，我们有一个词，sambadrome。

segments.en: So it's a proper noun, not a common noun, right?
segments.zh: 所以它是专有名词，而不是普通名词，对吧？

segments.en: No, it's not really a common noun.
segments.zh: 不，它不是一个普通的名词。

segments.en: It's a proper noun, but it is a building.
segments.zh: 这是一个专有名词，但它是一座建筑物。

segments.en: And what happens in this building?
Basically, it's very similar to a stadium, but each end isn't closed off.
segments.zh: 基本上，它与体育场非常相似，但每一端都没有关闭。

segments.en: So you have stands on one side and stands on the other.
segments.zh: 所以你的一侧有支架，另一侧站立。

segments.en: And you have like a little street in the middle.
So you can sit down and you can watch people parade or walk by, and you can see the dancers and everything.
segments.zh: 所以你可以坐下来，你可以看着人们游行或走过，你可以看到舞者和一切。

segments.en: And so what is it used for?
segments.zh: 那么它是用来做什么的呢？

segments.en: The Sambadrome is used so that the Samba schools can present their dances and their dancers and their costumes to judges and all the people that want to watch them dance Samba.
segments.zh: Sambadrome 的使用是为了让 Samba 学校可以向评委和所有想看他们跳桑巴舞的人展示他们的舞蹈、舞者和服装。

segments.en: Okay, so you've been using this word a lot.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你经常使用这个词。

segments.en: It's a dance that Brazil is famous for.
It's a very fast dance, a lot of hip movements, a lot of...
segments.zh: 这是一个非常快速的舞蹈，很多臀部动作，很多...

segments.en: It's very fast, but it's very, very nice.
segments.zh: 它非常快，但非常非常好。

segments.en: And the music is based with many different type of tropical instruments.
segments.zh: 音乐以许多不同类型的热带乐器为基础。

segments.en: I can Samba a little bit.
It's trickier than what it seems.
Okay, well, we're actually going to hear some Samba music in the dialogue, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，我们实际上会在对话中听到一些桑巴音乐，对吧？

segments.en: And we're going to hear some Samba that is actually used during Carnival.
segments.zh: 我们将听到一些在狂欢节期间实际使用的桑巴舞。

segments.zh: 好的，让我们现在去里约听一些桑巴舞。

segments.en: This is like a once in a lifetime opportunity.
segments.zh: 这可是千载难逢的机会。

segments.en: We're here at the biggest party in the world.
segments.zh: 我们就在世界上最大的狂欢派对现场！

segments.en: We're so lucky we found tickets for the Sambadrome.
segments.zh: 能买到桑巴大道看台的门票，真是太幸运了。

segments.zh: 不过我不认为他的妻子很高兴。

segments.en: Our first word on Language Takeaway today, ticket scalper.
segments.zh: 我们今天关于语言外卖的第一个词，Ticket Scalper。

segments.en: This is actually a job title, I think.
segments.zh: 我认为这实际上是一个职位。

segments.en: Maybe not a totally legal job title.
segments.zh: 也许不是一个完全合法的职位。

segments.en: So what does a ticket scalper do?
segments.zh: 那么票务黄牛是做什么的呢？

segments.en: Basically this person will sell tickets at a higher price to people who don't have tickets.
segments.zh: 基本上这个人会以更高的价格向没有门票的人出售门票。

segments.en: So he buys like 100 tickets and goes and stands outside of the Samba Dome or the...
segments.zh: 所以他买了 100 张票，然后站在桑巴穹顶或...

segments.en: And he sells them for like twice the price, right?
segments.zh: 他以两倍的价格出售它们，对吧？

segments.en: So basically they come in handy sometimes because you want to go to a concert or something and you don't have tickets, you got to turn to them, right?
segments.zh: 所以基本上它们有时会派上用场，因为你想去听音乐会什么的，但你没有门票，你必须求助于他们，对吧？
我们的下一个词，有声望。

segments.en: Now, this is a very nice word, prestigious.
segments.zh: 现在，这是一个非常好的词，有声望。

segments.en: Before we explain anything, let's listen to some examples.
segments.zh: 在我们解释任何事情之前，让我们听听一些例子。

segments.en: Harvard University is one of the most prestigious schools in North America.
segments.zh: 哈佛大学是北美最负盛名的学校之一。

segments.en: The Academy Award is the most prestigious prize an actor can get in the film industry.
segments.zh: 奥斯卡奖是演员在电影界获得的最负盛名的奖项。

segments.en: He worked really hard and now he is a very prestigious heart surgeon.
segments.zh: 他工作非常努力，现在他是一位非常有声望的心脏外科医生。

segments.en: I can see that when something is prestigious, it's really well-respected, right?
segments.zh: 我可以看到，当某件事有声望时，它真的很受人尊敬，对吧？
这是众所周知的，受人尊敬的。

segments.en: And if you are part of this thing, you can feel a sense of pride.
segments.zh: 如果你是这件事的一部分，你会感到自豪。

segments.zh: 所以基本上，这是四旬期的开始，这是复活节前天主教的这段时间。

segments.en: But carnival in Brazil is very special because of all the dancing and all of this and costumes and everything.
segments.zh: 但巴西的狂欢节非常特别，因为所有的舞蹈和所有这些以及服装和一切。

segments.en: Yeah, well, from the dialogue, it sounds really wild and crazy.
